ranges: SPDX and imports connect Arrow extension-name metadata, core Dictionary/Encoding/Field/LogicalType/Schema, Error/Result, HashMap and generated file protobuf. These conversions are shared schema boundaries, not an encoding implementation.

From<&pb::Field> is infallible despite the clippy allowance. Clone metadata keys and decode byte values with UTF-8 replacement, losing invalid original bytes. A nonempty dedicated extension_name overwrites the same metadata key; an empty dedicated name leaves an existing metadata extension intact.

Copy name/id/parent_id/nullability, wrap the logical type string, map numeric encodings 1 Plain,2 VarBinary,3 Dictionary,4 RLE and every other value to None. Start with no children and convert optional dictionary location; pb r#type is ignored. No logical-type, ID, encoding or dictionary-bound validation is performed here.

Primary-key position is Some(positive position), else Some(0) if the legacy primary-key boolean is true, else None. Clustering position is Some only for a positive position; its legacy boolean is ignored. These branches preserve primary-key legacy presence while clustering position zero decodes absent. Closing braces finish the field decoder.

From<&Field> for pb::Field copies IDs/name/logical-type/nullability, encodes string metadata as UTF-8 bytes and dictionary location, and maps the four Encoding variants to1..4, None to0. It does not recursively emit children; Fields handles flattening separately.

The protobuf field separately stores extension_name from core metadata or empty, forces r#type=0, sets legacy primary-key bool from Option presence and stores its position or0. It always writes legacy clustering bool=false and position or0. Core Some(0) primary survives via bool; Some(0) clustering would lose presence. No mutation of input.
Public tuple Fields owns Vec<pb::Field>. Private FieldNode owns one childless core Field plus child arena indices. No derives or validation occur in these declarations.

first_field_index_by_id iteratively traverses roots and children in pre-order using a LIFO stack populated in reverse order. Return first matching field ID, else None. Each call reserves up to all arena nodes and may scan all; it trusts internal indices. This reproduces the historical tree tie-break when duplicate IDs make a map lookup ambiguous.

From<&Field> for Fields recursively emits the parent followed by each child subtree in order, extending from newly built child Vecs. IDs/parent_id are retained, not reassigned or repaired. Deep trees still use recursive encoding and repeatedly move descendants through intermediate vectors; iterative decoding does not make all schema operations stack-safe.

TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema documents a flat pre-order list with parents before children, historical duplicates and legacy first-preorder matching. The compiling-style example reconstructs a single int32 root id0,parent-1 named value and asserts its name. Error associated type is core Error. The implementation actually requires earlier parents, not strictly contiguous pre-order input.

Preallocate nodes, root indices and HashMap<i32,Option<usize>> to input length. For each protobuf field, parent_id=-1 marks a root. Unique prior parent ID uses the constant-time map entry; duplicate marker None invokes DFS. Missing parent returns Schema with child name/id/parent and earlier-parent requirement. An impossible ambiguous-map/no-arena match returns Internal. Parent lookup happens before inserting this field, so no forward/self-new parent is accepted; referencing an earlier node with the same ID is possible.

Attach new arena index to parent or root list, convert the protobuf field, and insert its ID into the map. The second and every subsequent occurrence change the map entry to None, permanently marking ambiguity. Duplicate IDs are retained instead of rejected. Parent/root and child order are insertion order; valid unique-ID construction is expected linear hash-map work plus payload copies, while repeated ambiguous parents may make reconstruction quadratic.

Allocate Option<Field> slots and materialize nodes in reverse insertion order. Reserve each child list, take already built children in recorded order and set the parent slot. Missing/already-taken child is Internal with node index. Earlier-parent construction guarantees child indices are greater for normal inputs. No recursive reconstruction, but Field destruction and other consumers may still recurse.

Take root slots in recorded order, returning Internal if unexpectedly absent; collect through Result and return Schema with an empty metadata map. Empty field input yields an empty schema. No Schema::validate, uniqueness/type/nullability/key validation or parent-ID normalization follows reconstruction. Conversion errors discard temporary arena state without external effects.

Public FieldsWithMeta owns Fields plus HashMap<String,Vec<u8>> schema metadata, both public. TryFrom owned wrapper has core Error. Example supplies no fields and owner=lance bytes, then asserts decoded schema metadata; it does not validate a nonempty schema.

Owned schema metadata keys are moved and byte values lossily converted to strings before fallible field reconstruction. On success use its fields plus converted metadata, replacing the empty metadata map. Invalid UTF-8 is replacement-decoded; a later missing-parent error drops the converted metadata.

From<&Schema> for Fields flattens each top-level field subtree in order. From<&Schema> for FieldsWithMeta uses that flattening and clones the entire string metadata map before consuming values into bytes. Neither assigns IDs nor validates the input; there is no fallible result.

Dictionary protobuf i64 offset/length are cast directly to usize; values is always None. Reverse casts usize back to i64 and never serializes loaded dictionary values. Negative values/overflow/truncation are not rejected at this boundary; architecture width affects the cast. These are locations/counts, not loaded dictionaries.
Owned Encoding converts exhaustively to the matching protobuf enum, including RLE -> Rle. Unlike raw field encoding decode there is no unknown variant branch.

cfg(test) imports Arrow/core schema types and wrappers. Private proto_field helper sets id,parent_id,name,logical_type and leaves all other protobuf fields at Default. No historical fixture is loaded by this helper.

test_schema_set_ids constructs a,b-struct(f1,f2,f3),c Arrow fields, imports to core, flattens and asserts protobuf IDs exactly0..6. ID assignment comes from core import, not this flattening conversion. Does not assert parent IDs or roundtrip.

test_schema_metadata creates one int32 field plus k1/v1,k2/v2, imports core, encodes FieldsWithMeta, decodes and asserts Schema equality. Core Schema::PartialEq compares only fields (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878), so this test does not actually assert preservation of the top-level metadata map. Only valid UTF-8 values are exercised.

It asserts root count, every root ID/name, two-child count and both child IDs/names in order. No timing, allocation or logical-type assertion; source intent does not prove a performance bound.

It asserts both root/child shapes, pinning the historical tie-break.

No local tests for invalid UTF-8, unknown encodings, extension-name precedence, dictionary negative casts or primary-key legacy-position combinations. Module ends; no tests were run.

build_page_info accepts already-supplied PageLayout. Before pairing offsets/sizes, reject unequal vector lengths with column/page and both counts. A caller can supply a layout not decoded from this page; no cross-check is performed here.

Zip page buffers, reject every offset not divisible by PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64, collect fallibly and Arc-own descriptor slice. Empty pairs pass; zero size does not waive alignment. Construct Structural encoding with provided layout, page.length as num_rows and page.priority. No offset+size overflow, file bounds, overlap, buffer-size or row-count validation here. Temporary Vec drops on first error.

build_column_info rejects unequal column buffer offset/size counts then copies pairs into Arc slice. Unlike page/global helpers, this column-level pairing performs no alignment check. page_infos is supplied by caller and is not compared against metadata.pages count or content.

Require metadata.encoding (column-specific InvalidInput) and fetch pb::ColumnEncoding. Arc<ColumnInfo> records caller-supplied column_index, Arc page_infos, descriptor slice and encoding. Column encoding grammar/version is not validated here; descriptor allocation occurs before encoding decode and drops on error.

validate_global_buffers iterates positions and rejects first unaligned position with zero-based buffer index/position/alignment. Empty buffers succeeds. Size, overlap, offset+size overflow and total file bounds are not inspected. No IO.

Private field_column_shape returns contributes=true,recurse=false for Blob/packed, otherwise children-empty versus nonempty. Public physical_column_count mirrors this: one for Blob/packed/leaf (including an empty struct), otherwise sum descendants without a parent header. Child shape, not only logical type, drives physical mapping. Recursion and unchecked usize sums have no local bound.

append_physical_fields recursively emits only leaves or opaque Blob/packed fields in source order, records existing i32 field ID and successive i32 counter then increments. Containers with children get no map entry. Public data_file_columns begins two empty vectors/counter0. Empty schema returns empty pair, no IDs assigned or validated; signed overflow not checked.

field_id_to_column_index zips owned mappings, filters negative column_index (not negative field ID), casts to u32 and collects BTreeMap. Duplicate field IDs overwrite earlier entries; negative field IDs cast. Normal nonoverflowed numbering is nonnegative, but no schema validation is added.

append_field_ids walks same shape, looks up contributing field.id as u32 and pushes found column index; absent IDs are silently omitted. Recursion is suppressed for opaque fields. It preserves schema traversal order and does not sort or deduplicate mapped columns.

projection_from_field_ids is infallible: collect mapped columns and Arc-own a complete schema clone. Missing mappings do not remove corresponding schema fields, so later projection length validation can fail or mismap if caller supplied inconsistent mapping. It does not prune schema or verify rectangularity.

projection_from_column_names first core schema.project(names)? then uses caller mapping with that schema. Errors from name projection propagate; no independent mapping validation. Private children_share_parent_length returns only logical_type.is_struct(); list-like children are intentionally not assumed to share parent row count.

validate_field_length accepts comparable flag, index list, shared mutable cursor and fallible column-length closure. For a contributing field consume next index or InvalidInput naming the field; increment cursor before invoking column_len(index as usize). Leaf/Blob/packed lengths come from that physical column; first error returns immediately.

For a recursing container, enforce_children = comparable && logical struct. Recurse with this flag and common cursor; first returned child length initializes field_rows. If enforced, any later child mismatch errors naming parent, child, actual and expected rows. Once a nonstruct ancestor makes comparable false, descendant structs do not reenable comparison. Container reports first child length; it does not multiply/divide list sizes or compute offsets. No resulting length gives maps-to-no-columns InvalidInput. Recursive depth unbounded locally.

prepared_read_length closure indexes prepared.column_infos by supplied decoder index, errors with index/available count if out of range, then calls normalized_column_num_rows. Contextual helper uses checked u64 sums and sparse first structural layer num_slots when present, otherwise page.num_rows (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:539-561). Pass decoder schema and indices to projection_length; no I/O in this path.

projection_length starts cursor0, reserves top-level length pairs, validates every field with comparable=true and stores borrowed name/length. After traversal reject surplus indices with supplied/required counts. Then verify_uniform_lengths enforces equal top-level lengths (empty schema+emptyindices =>0), contextual helper lists mismatching names/lengths (rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:563-577). It does not independently reject duplicate column indices or zero fields.

DecodeColumn is a plain fn(u32,&pbfile::ColumnMetadata)->Result<Arc<ColumnInfo>> type alias; capturing closures cannot be stored. Private Debug StructuralReadProjection owns that function pointer. read_projection wraps it in Arc<dyn ReadProjection>; exact grammar selection is injected without a version enum in this struct.

async_trait ReadProjection impl: validate_indexed first calls provider structural validator, then requires projection_matches_indexed_metadata, else returns provider indexed_projection_error. read_length directly calls prepared_read_length. No metadata is fetched by these two methods.

Async prepare Full branch validates projection against metadata and clones column_infos plus ReaderProjection. Shared metadata/schema allocations may remain Arc-shared; it does not decode/revalidate each column here or read disk. Validation errors abort before preparation.

Indexed branch validates projection, awaits load_indexed_column_infos with exact decode fn, IO/cache and original column indices, then builds decoder projection with same schema Arc but dense 0..N indices cast to u32 in requested order. Metadata loader must return correspondingly ordered infos. After either branch, calculate read_length and return tuple; length failure can occur after indexed IO/cache work. No rollback/cancellation guard/spawn here; loader cache/concurrency/IO lifecycle remains delegated.

It is a helper, not an executing test, and supplies no local fixtures/assertions. This file has no unsafe blocks or inline test cases.

Private required borrows Option<&T>, returns the same reference or InvalidInput source naming Lance v2.3, supplied label and missing nested encoding. It does not clone payloads or supply defaults.

Private validate_compressive_encoding requires compression oneof. Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant immediately succeed without inspecting bit widths/data fields/literal size. Variable requires/revalidates offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking requires/revalidates values; Fsst likewise values. Local recursive validation has no explicit depth limit; external protobuf decode limits remain a separate concern.

Dictionary first requires and recursively validates indices, then items. Missing/invalid indices short-circuit before items. num_dictionary_items and index/value relationships are not checked. This is grammar validation, not decoding data bytes.

RLE now recursively validates required values then required run lengths using full v2.3 grammar; direct Flat8 run lengths and fixed flat values are no longer mandatory here. ByteStreamSplit/General/FixedSizeList/PackedStruct likewise require/revalidate values only. No numeric width/domain/codec fields are checked on accepted leaf nodes.

VariablePackedStruct requires each field.value and recursively validates, first failure stops; empty fields accepted. Missing compression oneof returns v2.3 InvalidInput. Logical schema/child count and value decoding are outside this function.

validate_sparse_positions inspects only a present Positions::Explicit encoding and applies compressive validation; absent SparsePositionSet, absent positions oneof and nonexplicit variants all succeed. validate_sparse_validity does nothing for absent validity, otherwise delegates its optional positions. It does not require a complete set representation or check position ordering/count/range.

validate_sparse_layout first requires has_large_chunk=true, then required/validated value_compression. Iterate structural layers; Validity layer checks only optional validity set via helper. No check that layers is nonempty, num_slots agrees with row count or sparse data exists.

List layer validates optional non_empty_positions, only explicit counts encoding, then optional validity. Absent count set/oneof and nonexplicit counts pass. FixedSizeList checks only optional validity. Missing structural layer variant returns InvalidInput; all layers otherwise complete with Ok. Fixed-size dimension/counts/slot arithmetic are not checked here.

validate_page_layout MiniBlock requires has_large_chunk=true then traverses optional rep, optional def, required values and optional dictionary in order. Error precedence follows this order; this dense page branch is separate from sparse layout checks.

FullZip validates required value only. Constant validates optional rep/def and leaves inline_value unchecked. Sparse invokes validate_sparse_layout; Blob requires inner_layout then recursive exact validation. Missing layout errors. No local recursion limit, file-bound/data-byte/codec-level validation or fallback to earlier grammar.

decode_column enumerates every page: shared syntax decode PageLayout, exact validate_page_layout, then shared build_page_info. First syntax/grammar failure precedes that page alignment checks. Fallibly collect pages then shared build_column_info decodes column encoding. No local ColumnEncoding variant validator, physical data read or schema comparison. Empty page list still requires a valid column-encoding envelope (rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:118-155).

decode_column_metadata enumerates and checked-converts zero-based indices to u32, decodes in order and collects Result<Vec<Arc<ColumnInfo>>>. Message says more than u32::MAX columns; actual guard is per-index and permits index u32::MAX. No parallelism; first error drops constructed Vec.

projection_from_field_ids forwards shared leaf traversal. Whole-schema projection first creates parent module mapping from entire schema. Name projection passes original full schema and its mapping to shared schema.project wrapper, so indices preserve original file numbering. Unknown mapping entries remain silently omitted until downstream checks; these functions add no new validation.

finish_metadata requires literal footer pair(2,3) before any alignment or grammar work; wrong pair returns VersionConflict with actual raw footer numbers and exact version message. Then validate_global_buffers and decode all column metadata in that order.

On success construct CachedFileMetadata moving raw schema, original protobuf columns, decoded infos, declared row count, descriptors, all four byte-accounting fields, file size and retained global bytes. Preserve literal major/minor; set exact ConcreteFileVersion::V2_3. Full metadata and normalized descriptors both remain retained. This function does not reconcile schema, total rows, counts, file bounds or byte-accounting totals and performs no IO.
validate_global_buffers delegates shared64-byte position-alignment check; no size/file-bound check at this boundary.

finish_metadata_index requires enum V2_3; mismatch uses actual enum standard footer tuple for VersionConflict. Matching identity then checks global-buffer alignment and returns index unchanged. Does not load/decode individual columns or establish projection eligibility/length. Global alignment error follows version check.
Private cfg(test) grammar_tests imports pb21 types and defines flat(bits) with data=None. No sparse fixture appears in this file despite v2.3 sparse validation code.

accepts_nested_variable_width_rle uses Flat32 RLE values with Flat16 run lengths, nested as Dictionary indices with Flat32 items/count1, then FullZip with defaults. It is structurally the v2.2 rejection fixture with opposite outcome; name variable_width describes broader grammar, not a constructed Variable encoding.

The sole test unwraps validate_page_layout success. It asserts local grammar acceptance only, not actual compression/decompression, offsets, data correctness or compatibility. No async/unsafe code and no source test execution.

Manifest derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/DeepSizeOf. Public fields hold schema, dataset version/branch, optional writer version, Arc<Vec<Fragment>>, aux/index/transaction positions, u128 nanosecond timestamp, tag, reader/writer words, optional u32 max-fragment high-water mark, optional transaction path, next_row_id:u64, exact DataStorageFormat, config/table_metadata/base_paths maps. Only fragment_offsets:Vec<usize> is private. Docs require fragments sorted by ID with gaps, but constructors/conversion below do not sort or enforce this; public fragments replacement can stale the private offsets. Dataset version, writer-library version and data-file version are separate values.

DETACHED_VERSION_MASK is bit63 (0x8000000000000000); is_detached_version tests it only. compute_fragment_offsets maps each Fragment::num_rows().unwrap_or_default(), chains final zero, and scans prefix sums into N+1 entries, including terminal total (empty list->[0]). Unknown row count contributes zero; ordinary usize addition is unchecked. It preserves fragment order and performs no row-ID mapping.

Default ManifestSummary has seven u64 counters. Consuming conversion to BTreeMap<String,String> writes exactly total_fragments, total_data_files, total_files_size, total_deletion_files, total_data_file_rows, total_deletion_file_rows, total_rows, all decimal strings. Type is pub in private module, not facade-reexported, though callers can infer the summary return type and use its public fields.

Manifest::new accepts owned Schema, shared fragment Vec, storage format and base-path map; computes offsets, starts version1/current WriterVersion, zero timestamp/feature words/aux position/next row ID, absent branch/tag/index/transaction/high-water mark, and empty config/table metadata. It does not inspect formats, assign fragment IDs, validate schema/carriers or perform IO.

new_from_previous uses supplied schema/fragments and recomputed offsets; increments previous version with unchecked +1, retains branch/high-water/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata/bases and refreshes writer version. It clears aux/index/time/tag/transaction references and preserves only STICKY_PAIRED_FLAGS separately in reader/writer words. It neither normalizes nor validates half-set pairs and does not preserve covered-index bit here. Caller must restore index metadata as comment states.

shallow_clone is in-memory: clones each Fragment, stamps ref_base_id only on base and overlay DataFiles whose base_id is None via referenced_lance_files_mut, and similarly stamps local deletion descriptor. Existing external base IDs remain. Inline/column metadata remains cloned; no files are opened/copied.

Shallow clone keeps source version/writer/aux position/time/high-water/offsets/next row ID/storage/config/table metadata, uses new branch and transaction_file=Some(input), clears tag/index/transaction_section, and allocates a new fragment Arc. It masks each feature word to covered-index bit OR sticky pairs, preserving each side independently. Source comments justify conservative covered-index retention; index metadata copy happens outside this function. Base map is cloned and insert(ref_base_id, BasePath(...,is_dataset_root=true)) can replace an existing entry without collision validation.

timestamp splits u128 nanos into remainder<1e9 and casts whole seconds to i64, uses chrono from_timestamp with unwrap_or_default fallback for unrepresentable date, then Utc. No error returned. set_timestamp actually accepts u128 raw nanos despite DateTime doc wording. config_mut/table_metadata_mut/schema_metadata_mut return mutable maps with no validation, persistence or feature recomputation.

field_metadata_mut delegates recursive schema field_by_id_mut then yields metadata or None. Deprecated update_config extends config with key overwrite semantics; deprecated delete_config_keys retains entries whose names are absent from supplied slice. No table configuration semantics are checked.

Deprecated replace_schema_metadata replaces whole schema map. Deprecated replace_field_metadata replaces selected field map and returns Ok, or InvalidInput with field ID if missing. The preceding no-op comment is inconsistent with the implemented error branch; document the error as behavior. No primary-key validation is invoked.

detach_sparse_inline_row_ids sums visible lengths of Inline row-ID payloads (not deduplicated, not created/updated versions). Returns unchanged if sum==0 or sum.saturating_mul(4)>=buffer_len, preserving exact quarter boundary. Otherwise Arc::make_mut obtains fragments and each Inline gets Bytes::copy_from_slice wrapped in a fresh InlineRowIds (new digest memo); other metadata unchanged. A shared fragments Arc triggers clone-on-write. Caller-provided buffer_len is trusted; whole original buffer release is not guaranteed while other owners/slices survive. Ordinary sum can overflow; multiplication is saturating.

update_max_fragment_id returns for empty fragments, otherwise takes maximum u64 ID then try_into u32 and unwraps (panic above u32::MAX). It initializes absent mark or raises it only, retaining historic high water after deletes. No Result or ID validation; a stored larger mark is preserved.

max_fragment_id returns stored u32 mark widened to u64 if present, otherwise computes maximum existing fragment ID, with None only for unset+empty. max_field_id compares schema max (default-1) with every field ID in base and overlay referenced files (default-1); includes dropped schema fields and does not explicitly filter tombstone or reserved IDs. No field IDs are assigned.

fragments_since rejects since.version>=self.version, including equality, with InvalidInput describing newer version. It uses since.max_fragment_id as threshold and clones current fragments with strictly greater IDs, or all if absent. This is an ID-high-water heuristic, not content comparison; docs exclude recycling and it does not validate common lineage/branch.

fragments_by_offset_range uses logical row offsets, not row IDs: binary_search start in cached N+1 prefix offsets, otherwise insertion index minus1, then walk fragment indices. Break when fragment start>=end OR fragment end<=start; append(start,&Fragment) otherwise. Unknown current length acts as zero. It does not validate/recompute offsets, sort, deduplicate equal offsets or explicitly validate empty/reversed ranges. Duplicated offsets/zero-length fragments may select a zero-length entry and break before later data; callers need valid coherent counts. Returned elements borrow fragments, despite doc return wording showing owned Fragment.

uses_stable_row_ids checks reader word FLAG_STABLE_ROW_IDS only, not per-fragment metadata or writer word. serialized builds pb::Manifest then encode_to_vec: raw protobuf bytes suitable for IPC/temp storage, not a complete on-disk manifest with footer/sections/dictionaries.

summary folds fragments: total_data_files counts base f.files only and total_files_size sums only known sizes of those base files, excluding overlays/deletion/index files despite broad docs. total_rows sums only known f.num_rows; deletion_file presence counts even if deleted count unknown, known deletion counts sum separately. total_fragments is Vec length; total_data_file_rows=total_rows+total_deletion_file_rows, not sum of all physical counts when some lengths unknown. Ordinary u64 additions are unchecked; no IO resolves missing sizes/counts.

Async populate_manifest_schema_dictionaries is a V1 compatibility adapter. Exact V1 delegates populate_schema_dictionaries(&mut schema,reader).await; V2_0/V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 are explicit no-ops. No version selector or writer-library comparison is used. Included doctest wraps an async Result function, not ignore; it was not compiled.

BasePath stores public id:u32, optional name, is_dataset_root:bool and full URI/path String. new assigns without URI/ID validation; extract_path synchronously delegates ObjectStore::extract_path_from_uri(registry,&path), propagating Result. Actual parsing/registry behavior is pending; no store initialization in this body.

BasePath custom DeepSizeOf children adds name children + twice path children + size_of<bool>(). This literally overcounts path allocation relative to normal one-string ownership and adds inline bool as a child; source gives no rationale. It is an estimator, not measured retained heap.

WriterVersion stores public library/version Strings plus optional prerelease/build metadata. DataStorageFormat stores public file_format:String and ConcreteFileVersion; new uses literal lance, getter returns exact enum, Default uses stable_file_version() resolved elsewhere. TryFrom protobuf preserves file_format without checking it equals lance and parses version via from_manifest_string. Exact mappings are now covered at rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-27 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-261; selector acceptance remains distinct from persisted strings.

ManifestBuildConfig is a data-only public Debug/Clone struct with auto_set_feature_flags, resolved timestamp_nanos, use_stable_row_ids, optional legacy mode/storage_format, disable_transaction_file, migration_next_row_id and Arc<SpilledRowLineage>. Docs specify sticky row IDs, overwrite-only storage override precedence, migration bypass and prefetched spilled sequences needed for rewrite/update; no enforcement/default implementation occurs in this file. Clock resolution deliberately belongs to caller; cfg(test) clock mocking in lance is a source comment, consumer implementation pending.

VersionPart Major/Minor/Patch is pub in private module with no facade reexport. Private bump_version increments chosen semver u64 component, resets lower components for major/minor, leaves prerelease/build intact and uses ordinary unchecked additions.

Private split_version parses semver, returns None on error, extracts nonempty pre/build as optional Strings, clears both in parsed object and returns clean major.minor.patch plus separate components. Docs include rc/build/invalid examples. No library check here.

Deprecated semver is a distinct lenient parser: split self.version at first dash, parse first three dot-separated components as u32 with missing minor/patch default0, return remainder after dash as optional borrowed tag. Extra dot parts are ignored, explicit prerelease/build fields and library are ignored; plus-build in patch can cause parse failure. It is not equivalent to full semver::Version parsing despite doc wording.

lance_lib_version rejects library != exact lowercase lance, parses self.version with semver, then when separate prerelease/build fields are Some parses and overwrites corresponding parsed components. None leaves components embedded in version string intact. Any parse error returns None. Arbitrary nonsemver WriterVersion values remain constructible; only this interpretation fails.

Deprecated semver_or_panic wraps old parser and panics with raw version on failure. older_than uses lance_lib_version().expect then compares against release major/minor/patch with empty pre/build, so prerelease ordering follows semver. Deprecated bump expects valid Lance version, increments numeric part, clears only prerelease if keep_tag=false (build retained), splits back to clean fields and clones library. Non-Lance/invalid versions panic; future-private wording is intent, not current restriction.

WriterVersion Default outside cfg(test) parses compile-time CARGO_PKG_VERSION and emits library lance, clean version and separate pre/build, panicking if invalid. Under this crate cfg(test), same fields then bump(Patch,true), retaining pre/build but using next patch. Dependency builds do not automatically inherit cfg(test); no actual Cargo version value is asserted here.

ProtoStruct maps Manifest::Proto=pb::Manifest. BasePath From conversions copy/move matching id/name/root/path fields, no URI/duplicate validation. Converting owned BasePath to protobuf consumes Strings.

Manifest TryFrom starts timestamp conversion by casting signed seconds/nanos to u128 then sec*1e9+nanos; absent timestamp defaults later to0. Negative or out-of-range values are not validated and casts/arithmetic can wrap/panic according to overflow policy. Any Some writer_version message becomes Some even with empty library/version; the fully-set comment does not enforce nonempty fields.

A fresh DataFileFieldInterner converts all protobuf fragments, sharing repeated base field/column lists and inline version bytes across this manifest, preserving fragment order. It computes logical offsets and wraps fields/schema metadata. If reader stable-row bit is set but any fragment lacks row_id_meta, returns Internal All fragments must have row ids; empty fragment set passes. It does not decode inline sequences or validate Column carriers.

If data_format absent, infer exact version from all base/overlay files, rejecting mixed versions; with no files use stable_file_version when deprecated writer bit2 set, else V1. If data_format present, trust converted DataStorageFormat without comparing per-file versions. Then convert schema via FieldsWithMeta. This conversion alone does not invoke ensure_can_read_manifest/paired flag checks or reject fragment_tree.

Final Manifest retains raw version/branch/flags/high-water/next row/config/table metadata, casts aux/index/transaction offsets to usize without checked conversion, normalizes empty tag/transaction_file to None, and collects base-path entries by id into HashMap (later duplicate ID replaces earlier). Uses converted fragments/schema/format and computed offsets. Unknown/ignored protobuf fields including fragment_tree have no Rust representation here.

Manifest->protobuf omits timestamp if nanos==0, else divides into seconds cast i64 and subsecond i32 without overflow validation. Converts schema through FieldsWithMeta and separately encodes schema metadata String values as UTF8 Vec; clones branch/writer strings including separate pre/build and converts fragments in order. This conversion does not validate inputs.

Output sets fragment_tree=None, preserves metadata/flags/high-water/counts, casts usize positions to u64, writes absent tag/transaction file as empty String, always includes data_format with exact to_manifest_string, clones config and emits base_paths from HashMap values in unspecified order. transaction_section presence retained.
